data.why: The app generates its own demo movie in-app (a synthetic calcium wave with known speed, selectable via the 'Demo (synthetic wave)' radio button), so no external files are needed; an upload path also exists for TIFF/mp4/avi/mov but is optional.

goals: Load a calcium-imaging movie (or the built-in synthetic demo) and condense it into a single interpretable temporal color-code image showing where and when activity occurred
Estimate the propagation speed and direction of a calcium wave from the activation-time map, with a reported planarity R2 and flow-coherence score to judge trustworthiness
Verify the automatic wave axis and ROI segmentation against the std-projection overlay before trusting any numbers
Detect active ROIs automatically, inspect their dF/F traces sorted by onset time to read off sequential recruitment
Tune accuracy controls (photobleach correction, F0 baseline percentile, coherence gate, denoise, gamma) to recover a weak or noisy wave without over-trusting a guess
Download a print-ready, 300 dpi composite figure (and the single-image summary) suitable for a publication

review.summary: The tree states exactly what the README says the tool is for (one image plus a speed you can defend, checked against the overlay), and every screen I sampled supports its node. It needs small fixes before filing: put the kymograph and verification phases in the right place, stop calling denoise a display control, and give the hidden settings behind three of the quoted numbers.
